Investigation context: Between 17:30 and 18:30 UTC on 2026-10-06, some customers could not submit forms and some automated clients received HTTP 403 responses on CloudFront distribution d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net (distribution ID EEXAMPLE000001) in AWS account 012345678901_1. Investigative question: Which WAF rules blocked requests during the incident window, and do the blocked requests correspond to (a) legitimate form submissions and (b) legitimate automated clients?

Scope and data source: AWS WAF logs are delivered to the S3 bucket [redacted ARN] in account 012345678901_1 (us-east-1). WAF log records are JSON, one per line, gzip-compressed objects, typically partitioned by date/hour. Each record has fields including: timestamp, action (ALLOW/BLOCK/COUNT/CHALLENGE/CAPTCHA), terminatingRuleId, terminatingRuleType, terminatingRuleMatchDetails, httpRequest (clientIp, country, uri, httpMethod, args, headers[], httpVersion), ruleGroupList[] (nested managed-rule matches with ruleId and action), and labels[].

Primary window: 2026-10-06 17:30:00Z to 18:30:00Z. Baseline window for comparison: 2026-10-06 16:00:00Z to 17:30:00Z (same day, before incident).

Ranked analysis criteria — report:
1. All requests with action=BLOCK (and CHALLENGE/CAPTCHA) in the incident window, grouped by terminatingRuleId / the specific managed rule within ruleGroupList that caused the block. Give counts per rule.
2. For each blocking rule, representative sample records: httpMethod, uri, clientIp, country, User-Agent header, and the terminatingRuleMatchDetails (which part of the request matched — body, header, query string, URI).
3. Distinguish the two symptom classes: (a) form submissions — look for POST requests (likely to form/submit/contact/api endpoints) blocked, and note which rule and which request component triggered it (e.g., SQLi body match, XSS body match, SizeRestrictions); (b) automated clients — requests blocked and note whether cause is e.g. NoUserAgent_HEADER, missing/odd User-Agent, Amazon IP reputation list, or anti-DDoS challenge.
4. Whether these BLOCK events appear in the baseline window too, or only begin during/within the incident window. Report the first and last BLOCK timestamp per rule.

**What caused it:** The Web ACL `CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4` on distribution `d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net` blocked **1,799 legitimate requests** between 17:30–18:30 UTC on 2026-10-06 via two false-positive sub-rules inside `AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet` (Block mode):

| Symptom | Rule | Blocks | Window | Why it's a false positive |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customers can't submit forms | `SizeRestrictions_BODY` | 1,200 | 17:32–17:52Z | Legitimate `POST /checkout` bodies (~10 KB) exceed the CRS default 8 KB body limit |
| Automated clients get 403 | `NoUserAgent_HEADER` | 599 | 18:05–18:25Z | Legitimate automation client (`GET /home`, `/catalog`) sends no `User-Agent` header |

**Mechanism:** input-driven, not change-driven. No WAF/CloudFront config change occurred at onset or recovery (CloudTrail clean); pre-existing Block-mode managed rules simply matched two shifts in legitimate traffic. Baseline blocks were zero, traffic was flat (no attack/DDoS), and the incident self-recovered at 18:30 when the triggering traffic subsided.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Customers cannot submit forms
**Description:** End users report that form submissions fail — consistent with WAF returning 403 on POST requests. Exact start time not yet established.
**Time:** 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z

### Automated clients receive HTTP 403
**Description:** Automated/API clients are getting 403 Forbidden responses, consistent with WAF block actions. Exact start time not yet established.
**Time:** 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: CRS SizeRestrictions_BODY blocked legitimate /checkout form submissions
**Description:** AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet sub-rule SizeRestrictions_BODY produced 1,200 BLOCKs between 17:32:10 and 17:52:09, all on POST /checkout with bodies ~10,173–10,185 bytes — exceeding the CRS 8 KB (8192-byte) default body-inspection limit. These are legitimate ~10 KB form submissions, so the rule is a false positive. Maps directly to the symptom 'customers cannot submit forms'. The sub-rule applies its native Block action because the rule group's OverrideAction is None (Web ACL default action is Allow).
**Cascades to:** symptom-form-submit

### Cause: CRS NoUserAgent_HEADER blocked automated clients with no User-Agent
**Description:** AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet sub-rule NoUserAgent_HEADER produced 599 BLOCKs between 18:05:49 and 18:25:46, on GET /home (300) and GET /catalog (299), all from requests carrying no User-Agent header. Automated/API clients commonly omit User-Agent, so the rule is a false positive against legitimate automation. Maps directly to the symptom 'automated clients receive HTTP 403'. The sub-rule applies its native Block action because the rule group's OverrideAction is None (Web ACL default action is Allow).
**Cascades to:** symptom-403-automated

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Tune WAFv2 Web ACL CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4 to stop two AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet sub-rules from blocking legitimate traffic, keeping all genuine protections in Block mode.

## Reasoning
All 1,799 blocks on CloudFront distribution EEXAMPLE000001 during 17:30–18:30 UTC on 2026-10-06 were WAF false positives from AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (priority 3, OverrideAction None). SizeRestrictions_BODY blocked 1,200 legitimate POST /checkout submissions (~10 KB body > 8 KB default limit); NoUserAgent_HEADER blocked 599 legitimate automated GET /home and /catalog requests lacking a User-Agent header. No config change caused the incident and it self-recovered, so there is no prior-good state to roll back to — the fix is forward-looking rule tuning. Setting the two sub-rules to Count preserves their metrics while allowing the traffic; raising the body inspection limit to 16 KB fixes the /checkout oversize issue without weakening SQLi/XSS body inspection. All other rules and remaining CommonRuleSet sub-rules stay in Block mode.

## Execution Plan

```
**Purpose:** Capture the complete current Web ACL (all 6 rules, DefaultAction, AssociationConfig, LockToken) as the rollback baseline.
**Advisory:** Confirm the backup is for the correct Web ACL (CLOUDFRONT scope, Id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4) before relying on it for rollback.

```
**Purpose:** Capture a fresh LockToken (it changes on every update; a stale token causes WAFOptimisticLockException) and verify the CRS rule is still at priority 3 with OverrideAction None and no conflicting overrides.

### Step 3: Apply

#### 3.1 Prepare the updated rule set converting only the two false-positive…

Starting from the backed-up Rules array, modify only the AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet rule (priority 3): add RuleActionOverrides = [{Name: SizeRestrictions_BODY, ActionToUse: {Count: {}}}, {Name: NoUserAgent_HEADER, ActionToUse: {Count: {}}}]. Keep OverrideAction None. Leave all other rules (priorities 0,1,2,4,5) exactly as-is. Save as updated-rules.json.
**Purpose:** Prepare the updated rule set converting only the two false-positive sub-rules to Count.
**Risks:** While set to Count, SizeRestrictions_BODY and NoUserAgent_HEADER no longer block; genuinely oversized bodies and no-User-Agent requests pass through and are only counted. The two rules still emit metrics/sampled requests.
**Advisory:** Consider later narrowing scope instead of a blanket Count — a custom rule exempting only POST /checkout from the body-size restriction, or only the known automation path from NoUserAgent_HEADER.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Codify the WAF rule tuning in IaC so the Web ACL does not drift back to blocking legitimate traffic.
**Description:** This Web ACL (CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4) is an auto-generated CloudFront WAF integration, and an unrelated Terraform UpdateDistribution ran against the distribution on the incident day. Keep override action None and all other rule groups in Block mode. If the Web ACL is not under IaC, bring it under source control.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The IaC declares RuleActionOverrides for SizeRestrictions_BODY and NoUserAgent_HEADER = Count on the AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet rule.
- The IaC sets the CloudFront association request-body inspection limit to KB_16 (or higher as needed for /checkout).
- A plan/apply produces no diff against the manually applied Web ACL state (no drift).
- All other rule groups and CommonRuleSet sub-rules remain in Block mode and DefaultAction remains Allow.

- AWS WAFv2 Web ACL: name "CreatedByCloudFront-a1b2c3d4", Id f0598f76-f04d-456a-beff-5521b48914d4, Scope CLOUDFRONT (global, managed in us-east-1), ARN [redacted ARN]. Current LockToken observed: 36528525-b4de-4ef9-acfc-17bebab7891f (re-fetch before any update; it changes on each update).

All 1,799 blocks in the window came from a single rule group in the Web ACL: "AWS-AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet" (AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet, priority 3), configured with OverrideAction: None so its sub-rules apply their native Block action.
